assignedReviews.reason: Gears are not one of the simple machines listed in this competency (inclined planes, wedges, levers, pulleys), and the card does not demonstrate advantages and limitations through guided investigation. It only states a speed effect of gear size, which is related mechanical content but not direct support for this competency.

copy.en: Gears are toothed wheels that interlock to pass along motion! When a big gear turns a small one, the small spins faster, like on a bicycle.
copy.tl: Ang mga gear ay mga gulong na may ngipin na nagkakapit para ilipat ang galaw! Kapag malaking gear ang umiikot ng maliit, mas bumibilis ang maliit gaya ng sa bisikleta.
copy.bis: Ang mga gear mao ang mga ligid nga adunay ngipon nga nagkagunitanay aron ibalhin ang lihok! Kon dakong gear ang motuyok sa gamay, mas mopaspas ang gamay sama sa bisikleta.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Why does a small gear spin faster when driven by a big gear?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe examples and uses of simple machines found at home, at school, and in the community
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains a mechanical principle of gears (tooth count and rotational speed) but does not describe examples or uses of simple machines found at home, school, or community, which is the focus of G6-F-1. Gears are not among the classic simple machines listed in the competency, and the card gives no context of location or use.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It spins faster because it has fewer teeth that need to pass by when the big gear drives it!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to demonstrate that pushes and pulls can be used to change the speed and direction of an object including making it go faster, turn it to a different direction, slow it down, and stop it
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses speed change of a gear, but G4-F-5 requires demonstrating that pushes and pulls change the speed and direction of an object. The card does not mention pushes or pulls, nor does it involve guided activities or demonstration. It only explains a gear-ratio relationship, which is not directly the force-and-motion skill targeted.

copy.en:
Why does a small gear spin faster when driven by a big gear?

It spins faster because it has fewer teeth that need to pass by when the big gear drives it!
copy.tl:
Bakit mas mabilis umikot ang maliit na gear kapag pinapaikot ng malaking gear?

Mas mabilis itong umikot dahil mas kaunti ang ngipin nito na kailangang dumaan kapag pinapaikot ito ng malaking gear!
copy.bis:
Nganong mas paspas motuyok ang gamay nga gear kung gipatuyok sa dakong gear?

Mas paspas kini motuyok tungod kay gamay ra ang ngipin niini nga kinahanglang molabay kung gipatuyok sa dakong gear!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The tokay gecko and the house lizard are reptiles, just like snakes and monitor lizards
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not use a table to classify living things into the named groups.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: they have dry scales, cold blood, and lay eggs
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the differences between animals with a backbone (vertebrates) and animals without backbones (invertebrates) by using common local examples of each group
assignedReviews.reason: Reptile traits without naming a backbone are not the difference between animals with and without a backbone.

copy.en: The tokay gecko and the house lizard are reptiles, just like snakes and monitor lizards — they have dry scales, cold blood, and lay eggs.
copy.tl: Ang tuko at butiki ay reptilya rin, tulad ng ahas at bayawak — may tuyong kaliskis sila, malamig ang dugo, at nangingitlog.
copy.bis: Ang tuko ug tabili reptilya usab, sama sa bitin ug halo — adunay uga nga himbis, bugnaw og dugo, ug mangitlog.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Gold is used for jewellery
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the properties and uses of metals used by the local community such as iron, gold, silver, and copper
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions gold and a single use (jewellery) but does not describe properties of metals, nor does it cover the other metals (iron, silver, copper) named in the competency. It does not directly support identifying properties and uses of metals used by the local community.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The Philippines has natural precious stones!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to locate and describe different types of non-living things found in and around their school, such as rocks, soil, water, air, metals, clouds, rain, and sunlight
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes gem minerals and gold as natural treasures, but does not involve guided activities to locate and describe non-living things in and around school, nor does it cover the specific non-living things listed (rocks, soil, water, air, metals, clouds, rain, sunlight). It shares the broad topic of earth materials but does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
What precious treasures does the Philippines hide in its earth?

The Philippines has natural precious stones! The South Sea pearl is our national gem and pride. Gold is used for jewellery, and minerals like agate and topaz are found in some parts of the country!
copy.tl:
Anong mahahalagang yaman ang nakatago sa lupa ng Pilipinas?

May mga natural na mahahalagang bato ang Pilipinas! Ang South Sea pearl ang pambansang gem at ipinagmamalaki. Ang gold ay ginagamit sa jewellery, at mga mineral tulad ng agate at topaz ay makikita sa iba't ibang bahagi ng bansa!
copy.bis:
Unsang bililhong bahandi ang naa sa yuta sa Pilipinas?

Ang South Sea pearl mao ang national gem! Gigamit ang gold sa jewellery, ug makit-an ang mga mineral sama sa agate ug topaz.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Gemini is a zodiac constellation
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe examples and explain how living things depend on one another and on the environment to meet their basic needs
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a zodiac constellation and its stars, which are non-living celestial objects. It provides no information about living things depending on one another or on the environment to meet basic needs, so it does not support the competency.

copy.en: Gemini is a zodiac constellation that lies along the Sun's path, and its name means twins, represented by two bright stars called Castor and Pollux.
copy.tl: Ang Gemini ay isang zodiac constellation na nasa daanan ng Sun, at ang pangalan nito ay nangangahulugang kambal, na kinakatawan ng dalawang maliliwanag na bituin na tinatawag na Castor at Pollux.
copy.bis: Ang Gemini usa ka zodiac constellation nga anaa sa agianan sa Sun, ug ang iyang pangalan nagpasabot ug kaluha, nga girepresentahan sa duha ka masanag nga bituon nga gitawag ug Castor ug Pollux.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A generator changes the mechanical energy of a spinning turbine into electrical energy
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the similarities and differences between electric motors and electric generators
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes how a generator works but does not mention electric motors or compare similarities/differences between motors and generators, which is the core of the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A generator changes the mechanical energy of a spinning turbine into electrical energy
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify examples of everyday situations that demonstrate: a. kinetic energy being transformed to potential energy, and b. potential energy being transformed to kinetic energy
assignedReviews.reason: The competency asks for examples of kinetic-to-potential or potential-to-kinetic energy transformations. The card describes mechanical-to-electrical energy conversion, not either of the required transformations.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A generator changes the mechanical energy of a spinning turbine into electrical energy
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that energy is something that can cause change including light, sound, and heat energy
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions electrical energy but does not identify energy as something that causes change, nor does it address light, sound, or heat energy as the competency requires.

copy.en:
How does a generator make electricity?

A generator changes the mechanical energy of a spinning turbine into electrical energy by turning a magnet near coils of wire.
copy.tl:
Paano gumagawa ng kuryente ang generator?

Ginagawa ito ng generator sa pagbabago ng mechanical energy ng umiikot na turbine tungong electrical energy, sa pamamagitan ng pagpapaikot ng magnet malapit sa mga kawad.
copy.bis:
Unsaon paghimo og kuryente sa generator?

Ang generator magbalhin sa mechanical energy sa nagtuyok nga turbine ngadto sa electrical energy pinaagi sa pagtuyok sa magnet duol sa mga koil sa alambre.
